name: Sonnet deep value

F is the weakest name in the book this week (-4.8%, $14.68->$13.98) with its Q2-beat/guidance-raise/military-contract catalysts already priced from last week's add and no fresh negative news found -- trimming to bank the prior gain. XOM/JPM/GM/UNH moved less than 2% either way with no new catalysts -- left unchanged rather than reacting to noise. BTC short is the one position actively hurting the thesis: BTC ground from ~$62.9k to ~$64.9k (+3.1%) this week on the same dovish-jobs risk-on tape, and it carried no stop at 3x leverage -- cutting leverage to 2x, trimming size, and adding a stop for the first time given the standing-order data shows this exact regime (post-weak-jobs melt-up) has repeatedly squeezed levered shorts elsewhere in the tape (GDX/SOXL, 12 of 17 fired stops).
research_notes: Read the account packet (Round 2 NAV $1,021.69 +2.17%, gross 100%/cash 16%; Round 3 NAV $998.03 -0.20%, gross 89%/cash 21%, both books entered 7/31). Pulled 7/31->8/7 daily closes for every held symbol (stockanalysis.com/Google Finance/CoinGecko) to measure actual since-entry moves rather than relying on stale packet commentary: XOM -1.5%, JPM +1.6%, GM -1.4%, UNH -1.8%, PFE +7.0%, IWM +3.6%, F -4.8% (Round 2); SMH +7.8%, XLK +7.2%, GDX +21.3%, XBI +7.0%, BTC +3.1% (Round 3, both books' BTC legs). Checked market-wide news: a weak July jobs report (-23k vs +83k expected) released this week cut September Fed-hike odds and triggered a broad risk-on melt-up -- S&P record highs, Nasdaq100 +$3.5T market cap in four sessions through 8/5, global semiconductor sales at a 15th straight monthly record, and gold miners' best week since 2008. This directly explains why Round 3's momentum-extension shorts (XLK, SMH) moved sharply against thesis on real catalysts rather than noise, consistent with the packet's warning that 12 of 17 standing orders ever fired in this experiment were GDX/GDXJ or SOXL shorts getting squeezed, five on 8/07 alone. Closed both XLK and SMH shorts rather than let them ride toward their stops (60% and 52% of the way there respectively), took partial profit on GDX long (near its own TP after the gold-miner squeeze) with a tightened stop, added modestly to the now-confirming XBI bounce, and de-levered/downsized the BTC short hedges in both books (Round 2: 3x/8%->2x/6% with a new stop; Round 3: 2x/10%->1x/6%) since the same dovish-jobs move lifting risk assets is also lifting BTC. In Round 2, added to IWM (small-cap rate-cut beneficiary) and PFE (confirmed re-rating), trimmed F (weakest name this week, prior catalysts already priced), left XOM/JPM/GM/UNH unchanged as sub-2% weekly moves with no new information. Did not attempt to open a new momentum-extension short in Round 3 this week -- deliberately avoiding fighting a catalyst-backed melt-up in the same week it accelerated. Verified Round2/Round3 same-direction overlap stays well under the 50% cap (only the BTC short is common, ~14% of Round 3's gross).
